olivia: RFC follow-up — quick sync on token-cost-aware admission for continuous-batcher. short goal: account for heterogeneous per-step cost without blowing up decision latency. thoughts?
sam: big +1 on accounting for cost. main risk is pre-enqueue estimation accuracy. model profiles help but we need fallback for unseen prompts.
jordan: one practical heuristic: estimate = length * avg_cost_per_token(model, decoder_state) + prompt_complexity_score. cheap to compute.
matt: tradeoffs: conservative estimates -> underutilized GPU; optimistic -> tail latency and budget overshoot. we need an escape hatch: emergency-slice or soft-evict.
olivia: interface proposal: optional field 'cost_hint' in enqueue proto. if absent, admission uses profile lookup. API sketch: { model, prompt_length, max_tokens, cost_hint? }
sam: example payload I had in mind:
```json
{
  "model": "rwft-13b-v1",
  "prompt_length": 120,
  "max_tokens": 256,
  "cost_hint": 480  // estimated compute units (optional)
}
```
jordan: also consider cost tagging: high-cost vs low-cost buckets. mixing in a batch creates stragglers. maybe enforce homogeneous cost buckets per microwindow.
maya: observability note — we should record estimated_cost vs actual_cost per request and expose histogram per model-version. that'll let us update profiles automatically.
matt: implementation constraints: decision path must be O(1) and <200us at admission. store profiles in shared memory on each host, avoid KV calls. decay per-tenant credits in background.
deploybot: :information_source: rolling canary deploy started for branch token-cost-admission -> canary group: runtime-canary-3, build: 0.35.2
olivia: action items: jordan -> proto sketch + queueing logic; maya -> telemetry counters + dashboards; sam -> run bench to gather estimate error distribution and propose conservative multiplier; matt -> emergency-slice design doc. also evaluate per-tenant soft-credit ledger for fairness. anyone want to own a short spike?
sam: I can run the bench today, will post numbers (error mean/std) and some simple multipliers. linking gist in a followup. :+1:
jordan: I'll sketch proto and add a unit test for estimate bias and a simple bucketed admission policy. will link PR.
maya: will add two counters: estimated_cost, actual_cost, and a delta_histogram; also expose a per-tenant rolling_avg_residual metric.
matt: note on batching: if we force homogeneous buckets we might increase latency for low-cost requests because we wait to fill a bucket. need to simulate throughput loss vs tail improvement.
olivia: perfect — let's reconvene after canary metrics. reconvene in the recurring runtime design sync next Tue. :coffee:
